title: What If Planets Circled a Dead Star? The First Ones Found Do

scenes.text: What if planets circled a dead star? The first planets we ever found do.
In 1992, astronomers spotted them around a pulsar, a star core spinning once every 6.2 milliseconds.
They found them by timing the star's pulses. Tiny wobbles in the beat gave the planets away.
One planet's year lasts about 25 days. The next takes 66 days, and the third about 98.
A star that dies in a blast should have wiped out its planets. These should not exist.
Scientists think they are second-generation worlds, rebuilt from the dead star's own leftover debris.
